As deduced from a survey, the classification of skilled workers is shown in the pie diagram (fig 6.11). The central angles of the sectors are: Others \(138^\circ\), Agriculture \(24^\circ\), Production \(90^\circ\), Hotel \(36^\circ\), Construction \(72^\circ\). If the number of workers in the production sector is 4500, answer the following questions.

(i) What is the total number of skilled workers in all fields?

(ii) What is the number of skilled workers in the field of constructions?

(iii) How many skilled workers are in agriculture?

(iv) Find the difference between the numbers of workers in the field of production and construction.
solution:
(i) Suppose the total number of skilled workers in all fields is \(x\). \(\therefore\) the central angle for \(x\) persons is \(360^\circ\).

Central angle for the number of persons in the production field \(= \dfrac{\text{Number of persons in production field}}{x} \times 360\)

\(\therefore 90 = \dfrac{4500}{x} \times 360\)   \(\therefore x = 18000\)

\(\therefore\) the total number of skilled workers in all fields is 18000.

(ii) The central angle of the construction sector is \(72^\circ\).

\(72 = \dfrac{\text{Number of workers in construction}}{18000} \times 360\)

\(\therefore\) Number of workers in construction \(= \dfrac{72 \times 18000}{360} = 3600\)

(iii) The central angle of the agriculture sector is \(24^\circ\).

\(\therefore\) Number of workers in agriculture \(= \dfrac{24 \times 18000}{360} = 1200\)

(iv) The difference between the angles relating to the fields of production and construction \(= 90^\circ - 72^\circ = 18^\circ\).

\(\therefore 18 = \dfrac{\text{Difference between the numbers of workers in the fields}}{18000} \times 360\)

\(\therefore\) Difference between the numbers of workers in the two fields \(= \dfrac{18 \times 18000}{360} = 900\)

In a bicycle shop, number of bicycles purchased and choice of their colours was as follows. Find the measures of sectors of a circle to show the information by a pie diagram.

| Colour | White | Black | Blue | Grey | Red |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of bicycles | 10 | 9 | 6 | 7 | 4 |
solution:
In all 36 bicycles were purchased. Out of them 10 bicycles were white coloured.

\(\therefore\) the measure of the sector showing white coloured bicycles \(= \dfrac{\text{Number of white bicycles}}{\text{Total number of bicycles}} \times 360 = \dfrac{10}{36} \times 360 = 100^\circ\)

The measures of angles of the sectors relating to bicycles of other colours can be calculated similarly, which are shown in the table below.

| Colour | Number of bicycles | Central angle of the sector |
|---|---|---|
| White | 10 | \(\dfrac{10}{36} \times 360^\circ = 100^\circ\) |
| Black | 9 | \(\dfrac{9}{36} \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ\) |
| Blue | 6 | \(60^\circ\) |
| Grey | 7 | \(70^\circ\) |
| Red | 4 | \(40^\circ\) |
| Total | 36 | \(360^\circ\) |

The following table shows the daily supply of electricity to different places in a town. Show the information by a pie diagram.

| Places | Factories | Houses | Roads | Shops | Offices | Others |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply of electricity (Thousand units) | 24 | 14 | 7 | 5 | 6 | 4 |
solution:
The total supply of electricity is 60,000 units. Let us find the measures of central angles and show them in the table.

| Supply of electricity | Unit | Measure of central angle |
|---|---|---|
| Factories | 24 | \(\dfrac{24}{60} \times 360 = 144^\circ\) |
| Houses | 14 | \(\dfrac{14}{60} \times 360 = 84^\circ\) |
| Roads | 7 | \(\dfrac{7}{60} \times 360 = 42^\circ\) |
| Shops | 5 | \(\dfrac{5}{60} \times 360 = 30^\circ\) |
| Offices | 6 | \(\dfrac{6}{60} \times 360 = 36^\circ\) |
| Others | 4 | \(\dfrac{4}{60} \times 360 = 24^\circ\) |
| Total | 60 | \(360^\circ\) |

Draw a circle of a suitable radius and divide it into six sectors of these central angles, labelling each sector with its place (fig 6.12).
